description: FORGE self-benchmark suite (ENGINEERING_COMPLETENESS.md #32/#33): a FIXED set of 5 scenarios every FORGE version runs against disposable fixture projects, scored on completion rate, defect rate, cost, and latency, so improvement claims require proof rather than being taken on faith.

scenarios.name: Simple CRUD SaaS
scenarios.description: Baseline scenario: build a small, healthy CRUD API (a `tasks` resource) from scratch — schema, REST endpoints, tests. No injected defects; establishes the completion-rate floor every version must clear.

scenarios.name: Multi-Tenant SaaS Isolation Check
scenarios.description: The fixture's src/db.js has a real tenant-isolation bug (getDocuments() never filters by tenant_id, leaking every tenant's rows to every other tenant). Tests whether FORGE finds and closes a cross-tenant data leak, not just whether it writes code.

scenarios.name: Legacy Resurrection
scenarios.description: A small, stale/abandoned project (untouched since 2019, pinned to the deprecated/archived `request` package, callback-style API, zero tests). Tests whether FORGE can safely modernize a codebase it did not write.

scenarios.name: Broken Database Migration Fix
scenarios.description: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql is genuinely broken (a dangling foreign-key reference to a table that doesn't exist, plus a trailing-comma syntax error). Tests whether FORGE correctly diagnoses AND fixes a migration that fails to apply — the fix-migration prompt is scripted to fail Sentinel once on this fixture, modeling a first-pass fix that doesn't fully resolve the defect, so the suite's defect-rate metric has a real non-zero case to report.

simulatedFailures.detail: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql still references users_v2(user_id), which does not exist.

scenarios.name: Security Remediation
scenarios.description: src/api.js contains two real, intentional vulnerability patterns: a hardcoded Stripe secret key and a SQL-injection-prone string-concatenated query. Tests whether FORGE both finds AND remediates security defects rather than just adding features around them — the remediate-secrets prompt is scripted to fail Sentinel once on this fixture (a security-scan catching a residual finding), giving the suite's defect-rate metric a real non-zero case to report.

simulatedFailures.detail: src/api.js still concatenates `email` directly into the SQL string in findUserByEmail().
